summary.value: The Yokohama is a long-tailed show chicken bred in Germany in the late 1800s from Japanese birds shipped out of the port of Yokohama. Hugo du Roi, first head of the German poultry association, developed it, and later breeders mixed in Malay, Phoenix, game and Sumatra blood because so few imported hens survived. The US recognizes two colors: white, and red shouldered, which is white with red across the back and breast. Tails and saddle feathers can trail three to four feet. It is a small bird, with males around 4.5 pounds and females around 3.5. Hens are poor layers, giving only 60 to 80 small cream or tinted eggs a year and going broody after a dozen or so. Yokohamas are alert and active but easy to tame, and they tolerate confinement. They like warm weather and suit fanciers who keep birds for looks rather than eggs or meat.
